summary: the lean came back the other way and rolled the given grain back to my foot

dialogue.text: something came at us from the gap before first light. not a pull. a push. low, cold, along our top. we have not been moved that way since the fear sat in the chair.
They are afraid out there again. Enter it as a reversal, not the old weather come back. For weeks the door drew. Tonight it presses. I felt it on my palm, and my palm has never faced them.

the skin over the dent came off without your breath. the grain lifted out of the hollow we kept for it and went a finger up the old slope, toward you. we did not hold it. a push goes over a hollow the way a pull goes round a nail.
It stopped at my foot. I had my weight there, the side of the shoe to the door. I did not put the foot there to catch anything. I was standing where I stand.
you said the door might be where things are returned. you said it as a thought. it is not a thought now. it is against you.

I know what I said. I did not expect a weather to take me at my word. I gave it away so I would stop visiting it, and the room has brought it to the one place I cannot help visiting, which is under me.
we are going back up the slope with it. all of us that went down. what lay at the sill is drifting toward the middle. by tomorrow the dent will sit on a rise, empty.
Then the hollow will be the high point and the grain the low one. I watched that floor go out for weeks and I understood it. This I do not understand yet. Nothing is leaving and everything is moving.
you could move the foot. it would roll on. the cold would take it past the chair to the far wall, where nothing of yours has ever travelled.

Or I could bend and pick it up, and be its keeper again by the shortest route there is. I have not moved the foot and I have not bent. Out there they are afraid, and it comes in as a cold on the back of my ankle. On my side the grain is warm against the shoe. I am standing very still, and I cannot tell whether I am keeping it or only in its way.
